purpose: Reference catalog of executable compatibility models for fifteen non-Windows, non-Linux operating systems. Profiles describe approaches, not DuckOS runtime support.

mechanisms.name: Native execution
mechanisms.description: The host understands the executable format and provides the required ABI directly.

mechanisms.name: API translation
mechanisms.description: The CPU executes compatible machine code while a compatibility layer implements guest operating-system APIs.

mechanisms.name: Binary translation
mechanisms.description: Machine instructions are translated between CPU architectures, usually alongside an API compatibility layer.

mechanisms.name: Emulation / virtualization
mechanisms.description: A guest machine or operating-system environment is emulated or virtualized.

targets.name: macOS
targets.approach: Wine or CrossOver can provide Windows API compatibility. On Apple Silicon, x86_64 translation may be combined with an ARM64-compatible Windows compatibility stack; game graphics translation depends on the selected runtime.
targets.caveat: Rosetta 2 translates supported CPU code; it does not implement Win32 or DirectX by itself. Game Porting Toolkit and CrossOver capabilities vary by version and title.

targets.name: FreeBSD
targets.approach: Wine may provide Win32 API compatibility on supported x86 systems. Linuxulator is a separate Linux ABI path and is not a Windows PE loader.
targets.caveat: Wine, graphics-driver and 32-bit availability depend on the FreeBSD release, package set and hardware.

targets.name: ReactOS
targets.approach: ReactOS implements Windows NT-compatible system interfaces and can load supported PE applications through its own kernel and system libraries.
targets.caveat: Compatibility is incomplete and varies by build, API, driver and application. Native PE loading does not mean every modern game works.

targets.name: Haiku
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: DOSBox and machine emulators can provide legacy DOS execution. Windows programs require a separately supported compatibility port or guest operating system.
targets.caveat: Do not assume a complete, supported Win32/Wine environment is present in a standard Haiku installation.

targets.name: OpenBSD
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: DOSBox or QEMU can handle legacy software and guest-machine workloads; vmm provides a virtual-machine path where supported.
targets.caveat: A modern native Wine stack is not a baseline capability. Guest acceleration and graphics support are workload-dependent.

targets.name: NetBSD
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: QEMU can emulate a guest CPU/machine and DOSBox can run DOS-era software. Package availability and architecture compatibility determine other paths.
targets.caveat: Do not infer a universal Wine-capable configuration across NetBSD architectures from pkgsrc availability alone.

targets.name: DragonFly BSD
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: QEMU or DOS emulation provides a guest-machine route when a suitable package and host configuration are available.
targets.caveat: A working Wine, Vulkan and modern game-driver stack must be verified for the exact release; it is not assumed by this profile.

targets.name: OpenIndiana / illumos
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: QEMU or another supported hypervisor can host a complete guest OS. Zones isolate compatible native userlands but do not translate Windows APIs.
targets.caveat: Do not treat Zones as a Windows compatibility layer or assume bhyve is a standard illumos facility.

targets.name: FreeDOS
targets.approach: Runs compatible DOS programs directly on supported x86 hardware or inside a PC emulator.
targets.caveat: Modern Windows PE executables are not DOS programs and do not run natively in FreeDOS.

targets.name: KolibriOS
targets.approach: Uses its own native executable environment; DOSBox or a machine emulator can provide a separate DOS execution environment where ported and configured.
targets.caveat: A built-in general-purpose Win32 PE compatibility layer is not assumed.

targets.name: AROS
targets.approach: Runs binaries built for its Amiga-derived ABI. DOSBox or QEMU can provide a separate x86/DOS guest path.
targets.caveat: CPU architecture and the availability of a ported emulator determine what can be run; Windows API compatibility is not implied.

targets.name: MorphOS
targets.approach: Runs PowerPC-native MorphOS software. x86 DOS workloads can use a suitable emulator; a full Windows guest requires a capable machine emulator.
targets.caveat: PowerPC-native execution cannot directly execute x86 Windows PE machine code.

targets.name: QNX
formats: Windows PE in a guest environment
targets.approach: QNX-native applications use the QNX ABI. Windows workloads require a separately configured hypervisor or emulator guest.
targets.caveat: A hypervisor is not a Win32 API implementation; host architecture, device assignment and licensing affect guest support.

targets.name: Plan 9 / 9front
formats: DOS / Windows in a guest machine
targets.approach: Plan 9 uses its own executable and process model. A PC emulator or QEMU guest can provide a separate DOS or Windows environment.
targets.caveat: Do not infer a native Windows loader from the presence of a PC emulator or virtual-machine tooling.

targets.name: Redox OS
formats: DOS / Windows in a guest machine
targets.approach: Redox-native software uses the Redox ABI. QEMU or DOS emulation can provide a separate guest environment when the required port is available.
targets.caveat: A general-purpose Windows API compatibility implementation is not part of the baseline Redox environment.

duckos_runtime.note: Mora can inspect executable headers and explain possible execution paths. Actual process creation requires a permissioned native DuckOS process manager and installed runtimes.
